The DMV is offering guidance for residents who need an official photo ID to cast their ballot News Shows Stations About Advertise Support Store Share Government

 1 min read The DMV is offering guidance for residents who need an official photo ID to cast their ballot
 By Todd Coppernoll , Adam D. Hess Oct 26, 2026, 1:33 PM CT
 Share
 As upcoming elections approach, the Wisconsin Department of Transportation (WisDOT) Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV) is offering guidance for residents who need an official photo ID to cast their ballot. Under state law, voters must present an approved form of identification at their polling place. Fortunately, standard Wisconsin driver licenses or state ID cards are fully accepted, and a federally compliant REAL ID is not required for voting purposes.
 To apply for a first-time state ID card, applicants should begin by visiting the official DMV portal at wisconsindmv.gov/idcards to review necessary documentation. Next, voters can visit their local DMV Customer Service Center with the required proof of identity, residency, and U.S. citizenship. While scheduling an appointment in advance can save time, walk-ins are also welcome at all locations.
 If a voter lacks the required documentation to obtain a standard ID right away, the DMV provides an ID Petition Process free of charge. This service issues a temporary receipt that is valid for voting while the full ID application is being processed, ensuring that no eligible citizen is turned away at the polls due to a missing ID card.
 For personalized assistance with obtaining an ID, residents can call the DMV’s dedicated hotline at (844) 588-1069. For additional questions regarding voter registration status, polling place locations, or general election rules, citizens should consult the official Wisconsin Elections Commission site at elections.wi.gov.
